scope: nested GNOME Wayland compositor availability and helper prerequisite probe

commands.assertions: GNOME Shell 46.2 started a nested Wayland compositor on an Xvfb backing display; the compositor socket and AT-SPI registry became available within the bounded run.

commands.command: dbus-update-activation-environment DISPLAY WAYLAND_DISPLAY XDG_RUNTIME_DIR XDG_SESSION_TYPE XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP; gdbus call org.freedesktop.portal.Screenshot.Screenshot
commands.assertions: The GNOME portal backend and org.gnome.Shell.Screencast activated and returned a Request object. AT-SPI exposed the GNOME screenshot permission dialog and the bounded probe could dismiss it, but the portal request did not return a capture before the nested session ended because PipeWire was unavailable to the portal runtime.

commands.command: PIPEWIRE_RUNTIME_DIR=<private> with a temporary pipewire-0 symlink to the active user PipeWire socket; gdbus call org.freedesktop.portal.Screenshot.Screenshot
commands.assertions: The private portal session could see an existing PipeWire core socket, but the GNOME Screenshot request still did not emit a Response before the bounded compositor run ended. This is an environment limitation, not acceptance evidence.

limitations: This is a bounded nested-compositor probe, not a primary-host acceptance run. It does not prove NAT-06, semantic accessibility, or the GNOME support row.

The nested portal could not complete PipeWire-backed capture even when pointed at the active user PipeWire socket; the result cannot stand in for a user-confirmed permission/recovery journey. The helper implementation remains fail-closed until a live grant and fixture flow are verified.
